source_steps.text: The representation carries brackets to operator commutators. H005 and H006 therefore give the following inductions. The h identity starts at hv=lambda v, and h y^(t+1)v=y h y^t v-2y^(t+1)v=(lambda-2(t+1))y^(t+1)v. For x the base t=1 is xyv=yxv+hv=lambda v. The step for t>=1 is xy^(t+1)v=yxy^t v+hy^t v=[t(lambda-t+1)+(lambda-2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(lambda-t)y^t v. In the h step L1 is the temporary hypothesis hy^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v. In the x step for t>=1, L2 is the temporary hypothesis xy^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^(t-1)v; its use of the h identity is justified by the completed first induction. Discharge each step hypothesis and apply natural induction. Thus F001 holds for all natural t, with the x formula used only for t>=1.

H003 gives lambda>=0, so |I|=lambda+1=n>0. Iterating F001, for i in I, x^i y^i v=i! lambda(lambda-1)...(lambda-i+1)v!=0: when i=0 the product is 1; otherwise all i factors of the descending product are positive integers and v!=0 by H006. Thus e_i!=0. To prove independence fix any coefficient family c indexed by I and temporarily assume L3: sum_(i in I)c_i e_i=0. For any j in I, apply product_(k in I,k!=j)(h-(lambda-2k)Id_V). The h formula of F001 kills every summand except j; its multiplier on e_j is product_(k!=j)2(k-j), nonzero over C. Hence c_j=0. Since j was arbitrary all coefficients vanish; discharge L3. H004 gives dim_C V=n, so the n independent vectors e_i form a basis.

Set z=y^(lambda+1)v. By F001, hz=(-lambda-2)z. Expand z in the basis F002; none of the eigenvalues lambda-2i for i in I equals -lambda-2. Applying h-(-lambda-2)Id to this expansion and using independence makes every coefficient zero, so z=0. Every higher lowering power vanishes. Dividing the identities in F001 by i! now gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_(i-1) for i>=1 in I, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<lambda, ye_lambda=0 and he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i.

Iterate F003 r times and divide by r!. If r<=i, the x coefficient is (lambda-i+1)...(lambda-i+r)/r!=binom(lambda-i+r,r). If i+r<=lambda, the y coefficient is (i+1)...(i+r)/r!=binom(i+r,r). If r>i the x string reaches xe_0=0, and if i+r>lambda the y string reaches ye_lambda=0. These are integer binomial coefficients, including r=0 where each empty product is 1. Together with F001-F003 these give all the asserted basis and operator formulas.

By H007, every X_r,Y_r preserves M. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M; H005 gives h=xy-yx as operators on V, so h also preserves M. Their restrictions satisfy the same commutator identities. H001 makes R the subring obtained by inverting integers prime to p. H007 supplies an integer basis of M that is a complex basis of V; N001 gives complex dimension n and |I|=n, so that basis has n elements and can be indexed by I.

Choose such a basis a from F001. Its tensor images 1 tensor a_i form an R-basis of M_R: the integer coordinate maps of a tensor to mutually inverse maps between M_R and R^I, sending sum_(i in I) d_i tensor a_i to (d_i)_(i in I). Under iota this basis maps to a_i. If a finite R-linear combination maps to zero, its coefficients vanish by complex independence of a. Hence iota is injective, its image is the R-span of a, and M_R is free of rank n. The image complex-linearly spans V because a is a complex basis. Each X_r,Y_r is complex-linear and preserves M by F001, so preserves this R-span.

Fix i,j in I. The basis formulas in N001 give Q=Y_lambda X_lambda=E_(lambda,lambda): X_lambda kills e_k for k<lambda and sends e_lambda to e_0, which Y_lambda sends back to e_lambda. They also give X_(lambda-i)Q=E_(i,lambda), since the surviving coefficient is binom(lambda-i,lambda-i)=1. Finally Q Y_(lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j)E_(lambda,j). Indeed an input e_k with k<j goes below e_lambda and is killed by Q; for k>j it goes past the lowering string and vanishes; and e_j maps with coefficient binom(lambda,lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j). These statements include lambda=0. By H001 and H003, lambda!, j!, (lambda-j)! have no prime factor p. The factorial identity lambda!=binom(lambda,j)j!(lambda-j)! then shows p does not divide binom(lambda,j), so its rational inverse lies in R.

Composing the three identities in F003 and using the defining action of matrix units gives E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1)X_(lambda-i)Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j) for every i,j in I. All factors preserve iota(M_R) by F002, and the scalar is in R by F003, hence every E_ij preserves it. F001-F003 and this formula establish all the asserted localization and matrix-unit properties. No weights modulo p were separated.

By N001, the e_i form a basis. By N002, E_ii projects iota(M_R) onto J_i e_i and E_ij carries c e_j to c e_i while preserving iota(M_R); therefore J_j is contained in J_i for every i,j in I. Reversing indices gives equality. The set I contains 0 since n=lambda+1>0, so the common module is J. Each J_i is an R-submodule, and multiplication by e_i identifies it with the image of the R-linear projection E_ii on the finite free module iota(M_R). Images of a finite generating set generate the image, so J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: if every coordinate projection were zero, all of iota(M_R) would be zero, contradicting its complex span V and dim V=n>0. Finally a vector in iota(M_R) is the sum of its E_ii projections, all in J e_i, and conversely every such finite sum belongs to iota(M_R); independence of the e_i makes this sum direct.

Define T=Q tensor_R J. Its multiplication map mu:T->C sends q tensor c to qc. It is injective by the fraction description of localization: any element is a finite sum of pure tensors, and a common nonzero integer denominator d rewrites it as (1/d) tensor c' for some c' in J, because d times each rational coefficient belongs to Z, hence R. If its product in C vanishes, c'=0, so the tensor is zero. This also exhibits Q as the fraction field of R and realizes T as the localization of the torsion-free module J inside C. The images 1 tensor c of a finite generating set of J span T over Q, so T is finite dimensional. Tensoring the finite direct decomposition in F001 gives Q tensor_R M_R isomorphic to product_(i in I)T: the forward map consists of tensoring each coordinate c e_i -> c, and the inverse adds the coordinate inclusions c -> c e_i. On pure tensors their two composites are the identity, hence on every tensor by linearity.

Set r=dim_Q T, a finite natural number by F002. Apply M002 with source B=R, A=Q and source module M_R. N002 provides its free R-basis of n elements, so finrank_R M_R=n and M002 gives dim_Q(Q tensor_R M_R)=n. The rings R and Q are commutative domains and satisfy the strong rank condition: for R, clear denominators to preserve injectivity after passage to its fraction field Q, then apply finite-dimensional linear algebra over Q; for Q use that same dimension inequality directly. Apply M001 over Q to the constant family T indexed by I. F002 supplies finite dimensionality and hence a finite basis of T, while N001 supplies |I|=n. Thus dim_Q(T^I)=sum_(i in I)r=nr. The isomorphism in F002 now gives n=nr; n>0 by N001, whence r=1. Together with injectivity of mu, J therefore spans a one-dimensional rational line in C.

F001 and F003 imply existence of a nonzero a in J and a nonempty finite list of nonzero rational scalars q_1,...,q_k for which q_1 a,...,q_k a generate J over R: start with any nonzero a in J, use the one-dimensional rational span to express a finite generating list as rational multiples of a, and discard zero entries. Each nonzero rational q_j admits q_j=p^(eta_j)u_j with eta_j an integer and u_j a unit of R. Indeed remove the maximal powers of the prime p from the nonzero numerator and denominator; their difference is eta_j and the remaining numerator and denominator are prime to p, making both u_j and its inverse elements of R. Thus the tuple of data specified in F004 exists.

Choose a,k,q,eta,u with the properties in F004. Define nu=min_(1<=j<=k) eta_j and b=p^nu a. Every generator q_j a=p^(eta_j-nu)u_j b belongs to Rb because eta_j-nu>=0. An index attaining the minimum has q_j a=u_j b, and u_j is an R-unit, so b lies in J and this one generator generates Rb. Thus J=Rb, and b!=0 since p is a nonzero integer and a!=0. F001 now gives iota(M_R)=direct_sum_(i in I)Rb e_i. The vectors b e_i are independent by N001 and b!=0 and span by that equality, so form an R-basis. N002 makes iota an isomorphism onto its image, which supplies the equivalent R-basis of M_R. Existentially close the witnesses; together with F001-F003 this gives all the asserted coordinate-module and basis properties.

By H001-H002, an integer denominator not divisible by p has nonzero image in K and therefore an inverse. Thus the integer map extends uniquely to bar:R->K, bar(a/d)=a_K/d_K. Define Phi:V_K->M_R tensor_R K by m tensor c |-> (1 tensor m) tensor c; define its inverse on pure tensors by (s tensor m) tensor c |-> m tensor (bar(s)c). The tensor balancing relations make these well-defined K-linear maps, and their composites are the identity on pure tensors, hence on all elements. Since p maps to zero, define Psi:M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/pM_R) tensor_(F_p) K by u tensor c |-> [u] tensor c; its inverse sends [u] tensor c to u tensor c. Changing u by p times a vector changes this by zero, and the F_p balancing relation follows from the R balancing relation and bar modulo p. Conversely R/pR=F_p because every denominator is prime to p, so every R scalar has the same reduction as an element of F_p. These maps are mutually inverse on pure tensors. N002 supplies preservation of M by all lattice operators, and H005 their Chevalley relations, so the actions rho and the operators X_K,Y_K are well-defined and all these tensor maps commute with them.

Choose b from N003, so b!=0 and the vectors b e_i form an R-basis of iota(M_R). Define a_i=iota^(-1)(b e_i) in M_R and beta_i=Phi^(-1)(a_i tensor 1) in V_K. The a_i form an R-basis by N002-N003. Its coordinate maps and the map (c_i) -> sum_i a_i tensor c_i are inverse K-linear maps between K^I and M_R tensor_R K; on each pure tensor this is precisely the coordinate expansion. Hence the beta_i form a K-basis. Likewise reducing the coordinates modulo p shows that the classes of a_i form an F_p-basis of M_R/pM_R, whose scalar extension gives this same basis via Psi. N001 gives |I|=n=lambda+1>0. Thus dim_K V_K=n>0.

N001 gives the explicit generator and divided-power actions on e. Complex linearity gives the same coefficients on b e_i, hence on a_i via iota and on beta_i after applying bar. Consequently x_K beta_0=0, x_K beta_i=(lambda-i+1)beta_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda, y_K beta_i=(i+1)beta_(i+1) for 0<=i<lambda, y_K beta_lambda=0, and h_K beta_i=(lambda-2i)beta_i for i in I. N002 gives preservation of iota(M_R) by E_ij. Define T_ij by the induced lattice action after pulling back through iota and extending scalars using Phi; then T_ij beta_k=beta_i if k=j and 0 otherwise. Transporting the equality E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1)X_(lambda-i)Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j) from N002 gives T_ij=bar(binom(lambda,j))^(-1)X_(lambda-i)^K Y_lambda^K X_lambda^K Y_(lambda-j)^K. This scalar is defined and nonzero, because N002 states that binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R and a unital homomorphism to a field maps units to units.

For any integer r with 0<=r<=lambda, H003 and H001 imply p does not divide r!, so H002 gives r! !=0 in K. The equality r! X_r=x^r on V restricts to the same equality on M by N002 and reduces to r! X_r^K=x_K^r on V_K. Division yields X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r, and the identical argument gives Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r. F001-F003 and these formulas prove all the asserted basis, scalar-extension and operator properties, existentially closing b,a,beta,T. When lambda=0, all factorials and binomial coefficients here are 1. No assumption on algebraic closure of K has been used.

Use H001-H002 for the prime-field/scalar identifications and H005 for the Chevalley construction. N001 and N002 supply the basis-defined matrix units and the restrictions of the lattice operators used in this construction, so all definitions of rho,x_K,y_K,h_K,X_K,Y_K are guarded by established inputs. Choose a basis beta and endomorphisms T with the full properties of N004. In particular dim_K V_K=n>0, so V_K is nonzero.

Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W of V_K and assume L1: W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K. It is then invariant under each nonnegative power of x_K and y_K, including power zero, and under their K-scalar multiples. N004 gives X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r for every 0<=r<=lambda. Every index lambda-i, lambda and lambda-j2 in the formula for T_(i,j2) lies in this interval, and binom(lambda,j2) is nonzero in K. Stability under composition and scalar multiplication now shows that W is invariant under every T_(i,j2), hence under all matrix units since i,j2 were arbitrary.

Split into the exhaustive cases W={0} and W!={0}. In the zero branch temporarily assume L3: W={0}; the desired disjunction follows immediately, so discharge L3 to close that branch. In the nonzero branch temporarily assume L2: W!={0}. Since beta is a basis from N004, there exist w in W, a coefficient family c in K^I, and j in I such that w!=0, w=sum_(i in I)c_i beta_i, and c_j!=0; otherwise all coefficients of every w in W would be zero. Retain this existence as F003 for the next paragraph.

Choose w,c,j from F003. For every i in I, the matrix-unit action in N004 gives T_ij w=c_j beta_i. F002 places this vector in W; division by the nonzero c_j in the field K yields beta_i in W. Thus all basis vectors belong to W and W=V_K. Discharge the nonzero-case assumption L2; together with the zero case this proves W={0} or W=V_K under L1.

Discharge L1 to conclude that invariance under x_K,y_K,h_K implies W={0} or W=V_K, and universally quantify the arbitrary subspace W. Combine this with nonzeroness from F001 to obtain the target conclusion. Since the Chevalley generators span L_K, their invariant subspaces are exactly the L_K-submodules. The endpoint lambda=0 uses a single basis vector with all relevant factorials and binomial coefficients equal to 1. By H003, for p=2 the allowed lambda values are 0 and 1, and the same formulas apply. No step separates h_K-eigenvalues or assumes K algebraically closed.

roots.statement: The field K has characteristic p.
With the representation act, V=V(lambda) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl2(C)-module of highest weight lambda and has complex dimension lambda+1.
L=sl2(C), and x,y,h are its Chevalley generators, satisfying [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h.
v is nonzero, xv=0, and hv=lambda v.

M is an admissible lattice in V: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and is stable under U_Z. M is arbitrary and is not assumed to be the minimal lattice.

For every semiring A satisfying the strong rank condition, every finite index type T, and every family B_t of additive commutative monoids with A-module structures that are free and finitely generated, finrank_A (product over t in T of B_t)=sum over t in T of finrank_A B_t. Here finrank is the natural-number value of module rank (Cardinal.toNat); the strong rank condition means an injective A-linear map A^a to A^b for finite natural a,b implies a<=b.

T has a finite enumeration.
Each B_t is an additive commutative monoid with an A-module structure.
Each B_t is a free A-module.
Each B_t is a finitely generated A-module.

All y^t v with t>=lambda+1 vanish. The generator matrices are xe_0=0; xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda; ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0<=i<lambda; ye_lambda=0; he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i for i in I. source_outputs.N002: M is stable under X_r,Y_r for every natural r, under x,y,h, and these restricted operators satisfy hx-xh=2x, hy-yh=-2y and xy-yx=h. iota embeds M_R into V; M_R is free over R of rank n and iota(M_R) complex-linearly spans V. Under iota, M_R identifies with the internal direct sum of J e_i over i in I; Q tensor_R J has rational dimension one and its multiplication map into C is injective. There exists a complex scalar b!=0 such that b belongs to J, J=R b, and (b e_i)_{i in I} is an R-basis of iota(M_R), equivalently its inverse images form an R-basis of M_R.
source_outputs.N004: There exists a K-basis beta=(beta_i)_{i in I} of V_K, so dim_K V_K=n=lambda+1>0. It has generator matrices x_K beta_0=0; x_K beta_i=(lambda-i+1)beta_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda; y_K beta_i=(i+1)beta_(i+1) for i<lambda; y_K beta_lambda=0; h_K beta_i=(lambda-2i)beta_i. There are K-linear endomorphisms T_ij of V_K for i,j in I with T_ij beta_k=beta_i if k=j and zero otherwise, and T_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1) X_(lambda-i)^K Y_lambda^K X_lambda^K Y_(lambda-j)^K. Here integer coefficients are mapped into K, every binom(lambda,j) is nonzero in K, and X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r, Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r for 0<=r<=lambda. The natural K-linear isomorphisms V_K -> M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/pM_R) tensor_(F_p) K intertwine these induced lattice operators; the first sends m tensor c to (1 tensor m) tensor c and its inverse sends (s tensor m) tensor c to m tensor (bar(s)c), where bar:R->K is the extension of the integer map. The second sends u tensor c to (u mod pM_R) tensor c.
source_outputs.P: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V_K, if W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K (the action rho of the Chevalley generators of L_K), then W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module.

result.text:
1: # Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
6: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
7: printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
8: \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
9: Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).
10: 
11: > 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
12: > prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.
13: 
14: ## Definitions and complete target
15: 
16: Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
17: \(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
18: Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
19: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
20: of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy
21: 
22: \[
23: [h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
24: \]
25: 
26: Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
27: \(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
28: the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
29: \(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
30: An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
31: subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
32: \(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.
33: 
34: Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
35: \(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
36: acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
37: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
38: Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
39: invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
40: Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
41: algebraically closed.
42: 
43: ## Fixed natural-language proof
44: 
45: ### 1. Divided-power coordinates in characteristic zero
46: 
47: Put \(n=\lambda+1\) and \(e_i=y^iv/i!\) for \(0\leq i\leq\lambda\).
48: The commutator identities give, by induction,
49: 
50: \[
51: hy^iv=(\lambda-2i)y^iv,\qquad
52: xy^iv=i(\lambda-i+1)y^{i-1}v\quad(i\geq1).
53: \]
54: 
55: For \(i\leq\lambda\), applying \(x^i\) to \(y^iv\) gives
56: \(i!\lambda(\lambda-1)\cdots(\lambda-i+1)v\ne0\) over \(\mathbb C\).
57: At \(i=0\) the empty product is one. Thus every \(e_i\ne0\).
58: Their \(h\)-eigenvalues \(\lambda-2i\) are distinct over \(\mathbb C\),
59: so they are linearly independent: applying
60: \(\prod_{k\ne j}(h-(\lambda-2k)\mathrm{Id})\) to a relation isolates
61: its \(j\)-th coefficient with a nonzero multiplier.
62: There are \(n\) vectors, the dimension of \(V(\lambda)\), hence they
63: form a basis. Also \(y^{\lambda+1}v=0\), since otherwise it would be
64: an eigenvector of eigenvalue \(-\lambda-2\), absent from this basis.
65: All higher lowering powers vanish as well.
66: 
67: The operator matrices are therefore
68: 
69: \[
70: xe_0=0,\quad xe_i=(\lambda-i+1)e_{i-1}\ (i\geq1),\qquad
71: ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1}\ (i<\lambda),\quad ye_\lambda=0,
72: \quad he_i=(\lambda-2i)e_i.
73: \]
74: 
75: Iteration gives the integral divided-power matrices
76: 
77: \[
78: X_re_i=\binom{\lambda-i+r}{r}e_{i-r}\quad(0\leq r\leq i),
79: \qquad
80: Y_re_i=\binom{i+r}{r}e_{i+r}\quad(i+r\leq\lambda).       \tag{1}
81: \]
82: 
83: The respective expressions are zero when \(r>i\) or
84: \(i+r>\lambda\), by termination of the strings just proved.
85: 
86: ### 2. Matrix units preserve the localized arbitrary lattice
87: 
88: Let \(R=\mathbb Z_{(p)}=\{a/b\in\mathbb Q:p\nmid b\}\), and regard
89: \(M_R=R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}M\) as a submodule of \(V(\lambda)\).
90: The embedding is injective because an integer basis of \(M\) is
91: complex-linearly independent. The module \(M_R\) is free of rank \(n\)
92: over \(R\) and is preserved by all \(X_r,Y_r\), by admissibility.
93: 
94: Define \(E_{ij}\) to send \(e_j\) to \(e_i\) and all other basis
95: vectors to zero. Formula (1) gives
96: 
97: \[
98: P:=Y_\lambda X_\lambda=E_{\lambda\lambda},\qquad
99: X_{\lambda-i}P=E_{i\lambda},\qquad
100: P Y_{\lambda-j}=\binom\lambda j E_{\lambda j}.
101: \]
102: 
103: For the last identity, an input index below \(j\) is sent below
104: \(e_\lambda\) and killed by \(P\); an index above \(j\) is sent past
105: the end of the lowering string. On \(e_j\) the coefficient is precisely
106: \(\binom\lambda j\). Since \(\lambda<p\), none of
107: \(\lambda!\), \(j!\), \((\lambda-j)!\) is divisible by \(p\), so
108: \(\binom\lambda j\) is a unit in \(R\). Consequently
109: 
110: \[
111: E_{ij}=\left(\binom\lambda j\right)^{-1}
112:        X_{\lambda-i}P Y_{\lambda-j}.                 \tag{2}
113: \]
114: 
115: Every matrix unit preserves \(M_R\). No assertion about distinct
116: weights modulo \(p\) has been used.
117: 
118: ### 3. Recover a standard basis for the arbitrary lattice
119: 
120: Define \(J_i=\{c\in\mathbb C:c e_i\in M_R\}\).
121: The coordinate projection \(E_{ii}\) maps \(M_R\) onto \(J_i e_i\).
122: Applying \(E_{ij}\) to \(c e_j\) shows \(J_j\subseteq J_i\);
123: reversing the indices gives equality. Let \(J\) be their common module.
124: It is finitely generated, being a projection of a finite free module,
125: and nonzero because \(M_R\) spans \(V(\lambda)\) over \(\mathbb C\).
126: The coordinate projections and independence of the \(e_i\) give
127: 
128: \[
129: M_R=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{\lambda}J e_i.                  \tag{3}
130: \]
131: 
132: One must still prove that \(J\) has rank one; containment in
133: \(\mathbb C\) alone does not imply that. Let
134: \(r=\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J)\), which is finite.
135: Tensoring (3) with the fraction field \(\mathbb Q\) and using the
136: rank \(n\) of \(M_R\) gives \(n=nr\), so \(r=1\), since \(n>0\).
137: The multiplication map \(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J\to\mathbb C\) is
138: injective: this tensor product is the localization of the torsion-free
139: module \(J\subset\mathbb C\), and a fraction mapping to zero has
140: zero numerator. Thus \(J\) spans a one-dimensional rational line.
141: 
142: Choose \(0\ne a\in J\) and write a finite set of nonzero generators
143: as \(q_1a,\ldots,q_ka\) with \(q_j\in\mathbb Q^\times\).
144: Each \(q_j=p^{\nu_j}u_j\) for \(\nu_j\in\mathbb Z\) and a unit
145: \(u_j\) of \(R\). Let \(\nu=\min_j\nu_j\). All generators belong
146: to \(p^\nu R a\), and a generator with minimal exponent generates
147: that whole module. Therefore \(J=Rb\) for a nonzero \(b\in J\).
148: By (3), \(b e_0,\ldots,b e_\lambda\) is an \(R\)-basis of \(M_R\).
149: 
150: ### 4. Reduce and extend scalars
151: 
152: All denominators in \(R\) are invertible in \(K\), so the integer map
153: extends to \(R\to K\). The natural tensor maps give
154: 
155: \[
156: M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\cong M_R\otimes_R K
157: \cong(M_R/pM_R)\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}K.
158: \]
159: 
160: For example the first map sends \(m\otimes c\) to
161: \((1\otimes m)\otimes c\); its inverse sends
162: \((r\otimes m)\otimes c\) to \(m\otimes\bar r c\).
163: The reduced images \(b_0,\ldots,b_\lambda\) of \(b e_i\) form a
164: \(K\)-basis, with exactly the matrices of step 1 reduced into \(K\).
165: The matrix-unit identities (2) persist on this basis.
166: 
167: For \(0\leq r\leq\lambda<p\), \(r!\ne0\) in \(K\), and the induced
168: \(X_r,Y_r\) equal \((r!)^{-1}x^r,(r!)^{-1}y^r\). Hence any
169: \(K\)-subspace invariant under \(x,y\) is invariant under every matrix
170: unit in (2).
171: 
172: ### 5. Conclude irreducibility
173: 
174: Let \(W\) be invariant. If it is nonzero, choose
175: \(0\ne w=\sum_i c_i b_i\in W\), and an index \(j\) with \(c_j\ne0\).
176: For every \(i\), \(E_{ij}w=c_jb_i\in W\). Division by \(c_j\)
177: gives \(b_i\in W\), so all basis vectors lie in \(W\) and
178: \(W=V(K)\). Since \(\dim_K V(K)=\lambda+1>0\), it is nonzero and
179: irreducible. If \(\lambda=0\), all relevant factorials and binomial
180: coefficients are one and the argument applies unchanged. For \(p=2\),
181: the allowed \(\lambda\) are zero and one; the proof still works
182: without requiring distinct reduced \(h\)-eigenvalues.
183: 
184: ## Input status
185: 
186: This file fixes the exercise, notation and supplied proof, including the
187: arbitrary-lattice argument. It is not an NL0 artifact, an Audit A receipt,
188: a Lean proof, or a passing test result. Future runs must construct and check
189: those artifacts from these explicit inputs, registering any foundational
190: module or localization results used by their NL0.

value.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
value.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V_K, if W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K (the action rho of the Chevalley generators of L_K), then W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module.

definitions.type: family of elements of the universal enveloping algebra U(L), indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: X_r=x^r/r! for every integer r>=0, with X_0=1. U(L) is the complex associative enveloping algebra of L. Elements of U(L) act on V through the extension of act. Juxtaposition such as xv denotes this action.

definitions.type: family of elements of U(L), indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: Y_r=y^r/r! for every integer r>=0, with Y_0=1, acting on V via act.
U_Z is the unital integer subalgebra of U(L) generated by X_r and Y_r for every integer r>=0.
n=lambda+1.
I={i in Z: 0<=i<=lambda}.

definitions.type: family of vectors of V indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: e_i=y^i v/i!=Y_i v for integers i>=0; only indices in I are used for the candidate basis.

definitions.type: subring of Q and hence of C
definitions.definition: R=Z_(p)={a/b in Q: a,b are integers and p does not divide b}. Ring operations are those of Q. All R-actions on submodules of V or C below use this inclusion.
M_R=R tensor_Z M, with scalar multiplication on the R factor.
iota(r tensor m)=r m in V, extended by the balanced tensor universal property. The R-module structure of V is restriction of complex scalars.

definitions.type: family of complex linear endomorphisms of V indexed by I times I
definitions.definition: For i,j in I, E_ij is the unique complex linear operator sending e_j to e_i and sending e_k to 0 for every k in I with k!=j. It is defined using the complex basis (e_i) indexed by I.

definitions.type: family of R-submodules of C indexed by I
definitions.definition: For i in I, J_i={c in C: c e_i belongs to iota(M_R)}.
J={c in C: c e_0 belongs to iota(M_R)}. When 0 belongs to I this is J_0; the definition does not assume that the different J_i agree.
V_K=V(K)=M tensor_Z K, with K acting on the K factor.
L_K=L(K)=(Zx+Zy+Zh) tensor_Z K, with bracket induced by [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h. These integral bracket formulas define the Chevalley construction including in characteristic 2.

definitions.type: K-linear Lie algebra representation of L_K on V_K
definitions.definition: rho is the action induced by the lattice operators: for t in {x,y,h}, rho(t tensor 1)(m tensor c)=(tm) tensor c, extended K-linearly to L_K. The action is defined when the lattice operators preserve M and satisfy the Chevalley relations.
x_K=rho(x tensor 1).
y_K=rho(y tensor 1).
h_K=rho(h tensor 1).

definitions.type: family of K-linear endomorphisms of V_K indexed by natural r
definitions.definition: X_r^K, also denoted (X_K)_r, is induced by X_r on M tensor_Z K: m tensor c maps to (X_r m) tensor c.

definitions.type: family of K-linear endomorphisms of V_K indexed by natural r
definitions.definition: Y_r^K, also denoted (Y_K)_r, is induced by Y_r on M tensor_Z K: m tensor c maps to (Y_r m) tensor c.
F_p=Z/pZ with its field structure for the prime p. For K of characteristic p its canonical embedding in K sends the residue class of an integer to that integer times 1_K.

15: # The Lie algebra `sl₂` and its representations
16: 
17: The Lie algebra `sl₂` is the unique simple Lie algebra of minimal rank, 1, and as such occupies a
18: distinguished position in the general theory. This file provides some basic definitions and results
19: about `sl₂`.
20: 
21: ## Main definitions:
22: * `IsSl2Triple`: a structure representing a triple of elements in a Lie algebra which satisfy the
23:   standard relations for `sl₂`.
24: * `IsSl2Triple.HasPrimitiveVectorWith`: a structure representing a primitive vector in a
25:   representation of a Lie algebra relative to a distinguished `sl₂` triple.
26: * `IsSl2Triple.HasPrimitiveVectorWith.exists_nat`: the eigenvalue of a primitive vector must be a
27:   natural number if the representation is finite-dimensional.
28: 
29: -/
30: 
31: @[expose] public section
32: 
33: variable (R L M : Type*) [CommRing R] [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra R L]
34:   [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [LieRingModule L M] [LieModule R L M]
35: 
36: open LieModule Module Set
37: 
38: variable {L} in
39: /-- An `sl₂` triple within a Lie ring `L` is a triple of elements `h`, `e`, `f` obeying relations
40: which ensure that the Lie subalgebra they generate is equivalent to `sl₂`. -/
41: structure IsSl2Triple (h e f : L) : Prop where
42:   h_ne_zero : h ≠ 0
43:   lie_e_f : ⁅e, f⁆ = h
44:   lie_h_e_nsmul : ⁅h, e⁆ = 2 • e
45:   lie_h_f_nsmul : ⁅h, f⁆ = -(2 • f)
46: 
47: namespace IsSl2Triple
48: 
49: variable {L M}
50: variable {h e f : L}
51: 
52: lemma symm (ht : IsSl2Triple h e f) : IsSl2Triple (-h) f e where
53:   h_ne_zero := by simpa using ht.h_ne_zero
54:   lie_e_f := by rw [← neg_eq_iff_eq_neg, lie_skew, ht.lie_e_f]
55:   lie_h_e_nsmul := by rw [neg_lie, neg_eq_iff_eq_neg, ht.lie_h_f_nsmul]
56:   lie_h_f_nsmul := by rw [neg_lie, neg_inj, ht.lie_h_e_nsmul]
57: 
58: @[simp] lemma symm_iff : IsSl2Triple (-h) f e ↔ IsSl2Triple h e f :=
59:   ⟨fun t ↦ neg_neg h ▸ t.symm, symm⟩
60: 
61: lemma lie_h_e_smul (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) : ⁅h, e⁆ = (2 : R) • e := by
62:   simp [t.lie_h_e_nsmul, two_smul]
63: 
64: lemma lie_lie_smul_f (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) : ⁅h, f⁆ = -((2 : R) • f) := by
65:   simp [t.lie_h_f_nsmul, two_smul]
66: 
67: lemma e_ne_zero (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) : e ≠ 0 := by
68:   have := t.h_ne_zero
69:   contrapose this

source_steps.text: The representation carries brackets to operator commutators. H005 and H006 therefore give the following inductions. The h identity starts at hv=lambda v, and h y^(t+1)v=y h y^t v-2y^(t+1)v=(lambda-2(t+1))y^(t+1)v. For x the base t=1 is xyv=yxv+hv=lambda v. The step for t>=1 is xy^(t+1)v=yxy^t v+hy^t v=[t(lambda-t+1)+(lambda-2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(lambda-t)y^t v. In the h step L1 is the temporary hypothesis hy^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v. In the x step for t>=1, L2 is the temporary hypothesis xy^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^(t-1)v; its use of the h identity is justified by the completed first induction. Discharge each step hypothesis and apply natural induction. Thus F001 holds for all natural t, with the x formula used only for t>=1.

H003 gives lambda>=0, so |I|=lambda+1=n>0. Iterating F001, for i in I, x^i y^i v=i! lambda(lambda-1)...(lambda-i+1)v!=0: when i=0 the product is 1; otherwise all i factors of the descending product are positive integers and v!=0 by H006. Thus e_i!=0. To prove independence fix any coefficient family c indexed by I and temporarily assume L3: sum_(i in I)c_i e_i=0. For any j in I, apply product_(k in I,k!=j)(h-(lambda-2k)Id_V). The h formula of F001 kills every summand except j; its multiplier on e_j is product_(k!=j)2(k-j), nonzero over C. Hence c_j=0. Since j was arbitrary all coefficients vanish; discharge L3. H004 gives dim_C V=n, so the n independent vectors e_i form a basis.

Set z=y^(lambda+1)v. By F001, hz=(-lambda-2)z. Expand z in the basis F002; none of the eigenvalues lambda-2i for i in I equals -lambda-2. Applying h-(-lambda-2)Id to this expansion and using independence makes every coefficient zero, so z=0. Every higher lowering power vanishes. Dividing the identities in F001 by i! now gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_(i-1) for i>=1 in I, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<lambda, ye_lambda=0 and he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i.

Iterate F003 r times and divide by r!. If r<=i, the x coefficient is (lambda-i+1)...(lambda-i+r)/r!=binom(lambda-i+r,r). If i+r<=lambda, the y coefficient is (i+1)...(i+r)/r!=binom(i+r,r). If r>i the x string reaches xe_0=0, and if i+r>lambda the y string reaches ye_lambda=0. These are integer binomial coefficients, including r=0 where each empty product is 1. Together with F001-F003 these give all the asserted basis and operator formulas.

By H007, every X_r,Y_r preserves M. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M; H005 gives h=xy-yx as operators on V, so h also preserves M. Their restrictions satisfy the same commutator identities. H001 makes R the subring obtained by inverting integers prime to p. H007 supplies an integer basis of M that is a complex basis of V; N001 gives complex dimension n and |I|=n, so that basis has n elements and can be indexed by I.

Choose such a basis a from F001. Its tensor images 1 tensor a_i form an R-basis of M_R: the integer coordinate maps of a tensor to mutually inverse maps between M_R and R^I, sending sum_(i in I) d_i tensor a_i to (d_i)_(i in I). Under iota this basis maps to a_i. If a finite R-linear combination maps to zero, its coefficients vanish by complex independence of a. Hence iota is injective, its image is the R-span of a, and M_R is free of rank n. The image complex-linearly spans V because a is a complex basis. Each X_r,Y_r is complex-linear and preserves M by F001, so preserves this R-span.

Fix i,j in I. The basis formulas in N001 give Q=Y_lambda X_lambda=E_(lambda,lambda): X_lambda kills e_k for k<lambda and sends e_lambda to e_0, which Y_lambda sends back to e_lambda. They also give X_(lambda-i)Q=E_(i,lambda), since the surviving coefficient is binom(lambda-i,lambda-i)=1. Finally Q Y_(lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j)E_(lambda,j). Indeed an input e_k with k<j goes below e_lambda and is killed by Q; for k>j it goes past the lowering string and vanishes; and e_j maps with coefficient binom(lambda,lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j). These statements include lambda=0. By H001 and H003, lambda!, j!, (lambda-j)! have no prime factor p. The factorial identity lambda!=binom(lambda,j)j!(lambda-j)! then shows p does not divide binom(lambda,j), so its rational inverse lies in R.

Composing the three identities in F003 and using the defining action of matrix units gives E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1)X_(lambda-i)Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j) for every i,j in I. All factors preserve iota(M_R) by F002, and the scalar is in R by F003, hence every E_ij preserves it. F001-F003 and this formula establish all the asserted localization and matrix-unit properties. No weights modulo p were separated.

By N001, the e_i form a basis. By N002, E_ii projects iota(M_R) onto J_i e_i and E_ij carries c e_j to c e_i while preserving iota(M_R); therefore J_j is contained in J_i for every i,j in I. Reversing indices gives equality. The set I contains 0 since n=lambda+1>0, so the common module is J. Each J_i is an R-submodule, and multiplication by e_i identifies it with the image of the R-linear projection E_ii on the finite free module iota(M_R). Images of a finite generating set generate the image, so J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: if every coordinate projection were zero, all of iota(M_R) would be zero, contradicting its complex span V and dim V=n>0. Finally a vector in iota(M_R) is the sum of its E_ii projections, all in J e_i, and conversely every such finite sum belongs to iota(M_R); independence of the e_i makes this sum direct.

Define T=Q tensor_R J. Its multiplication map mu:T->C sends q tensor c to qc. It is injective by the fraction description of localization: any element is a finite sum of pure tensors, and a common nonzero integer denominator d rewrites it as (1/d) tensor c' for some c' in J, because d times each rational coefficient belongs to Z, hence R. If its product in C vanishes, c'=0, so the tensor is zero. This also exhibits Q as the fraction field of R and realizes T as the localization of the torsion-free module J inside C. The images 1 tensor c of a finite generating set of J span T over Q, so T is finite dimensional. Tensoring the finite direct decomposition in F001 gives Q tensor_R M_R isomorphic to product_(i in I)T: the forward map consists of tensoring each coordinate c e_i -> c, and the inverse adds the coordinate inclusions c -> c e_i. On pure tensors their two composites are the identity, hence on every tensor by linearity.

Set r=dim_Q T, a finite natural number by F002. Apply M002 with source B=R, A=Q and source module M_R. N002 provides its free R-basis of n elements, so finrank_R M_R=n and M002 gives dim_Q(Q tensor_R M_R)=n. The rings R and Q are commutative domains and satisfy the strong rank condition: for R, clear denominators to preserve injectivity after passage to its fraction field Q, then apply finite-dimensional linear algebra over Q; for Q use that same dimension inequality directly. Apply M001 over Q to the constant family T indexed by I. F002 supplies finite dimensionality and hence a finite basis of T, while N001 supplies |I|=n. Thus dim_Q(T^I)=sum_(i in I)r=nr. The isomorphism in F002 now gives n=nr; n>0 by N001, whence r=1. Together with injectivity of mu, J therefore spans a one-dimensional rational line in C.

F001 and F003 imply existence of a nonzero a in J and a nonempty finite list of nonzero rational scalars q_1,...,q_k for which q_1 a,...,q_k a generate J over R: start with any nonzero a in J, use the one-dimensional rational span to express a finite generating list as rational multiples of a, and discard zero entries. Each nonzero rational q_j admits q_j=p^(eta_j)u_j with eta_j an integer and u_j a unit of R. Indeed remove the maximal powers of the prime p from the nonzero numerator and denominator; their difference is eta_j and the remaining numerator and denominator are prime to p, making both u_j and its inverse elements of R. Thus the tuple of data specified in F004 exists.

Choose a,k,q,eta,u with the properties in F004. Define nu=min_(1<=j<=k) eta_j and b=p^nu a. Every generator q_j a=p^(eta_j-nu)u_j b belongs to Rb because eta_j-nu>=0. An index attaining the minimum has q_j a=u_j b, and u_j is an R-unit, so b lies in J and this one generator generates Rb. Thus J=Rb, and b!=0 since p is a nonzero integer and a!=0. F001 now gives iota(M_R)=direct_sum_(i in I)Rb e_i. The vectors b e_i are independent by N001 and b!=0 and span by that equality, so form an R-basis. N002 makes iota an isomorphism onto its image, which supplies the equivalent R-basis of M_R. Existentially close the witnesses; together with F001-F003 this gives all the asserted coordinate-module and basis properties.

By H001-H002, an integer denominator not divisible by p has nonzero image in K and therefore an inverse. Thus the integer map extends uniquely to bar:R->K, bar(a/d)=a_K/d_K. Define Phi:V_K->M_R tensor_R K by m tensor c |-> (1 tensor m) tensor c; define its inverse on pure tensors by (s tensor m) tensor c |-> m tensor (bar(s)c). The tensor balancing relations make these well-defined K-linear maps, and their composites are the identity on pure tensors, hence on all elements. Since p maps to zero, define Psi:M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/pM_R) tensor_(F_p) K by u tensor c |-> [u] tensor c; its inverse sends [u] tensor c to u tensor c. Changing u by p times a vector changes this by zero, and the F_p balancing relation follows from the R balancing relation and bar modulo p. Conversely R/pR=F_p because every denominator is prime to p, so every R scalar has the same reduction as an element of F_p. These maps are mutually inverse on pure tensors. N002 supplies preservation of M by all lattice operators, and H005 their Chevalley relations, so the actions rho and the operators X_K,Y_K are well-defined and all these tensor maps commute with them.

Choose b from N003, so b!=0 and the vectors b e_i form an R-basis of iota(M_R). Define a_i=iota^(-1)(b e_i) in M_R and beta_i=Phi^(-1)(a_i tensor 1) in V_K. The a_i form an R-basis by N002-N003. Its coordinate maps and the map (c_i) -> sum_i a_i tensor c_i are inverse K-linear maps between K^I and M_R tensor_R K; on each pure tensor this is precisely the coordinate expansion. Hence the beta_i form a K-basis. Likewise reducing the coordinates modulo p shows that the classes of a_i form an F_p-basis of M_R/pM_R, whose scalar extension gives this same basis via Psi. N001 gives |I|=n=lambda+1>0. Thus dim_K V_K=n>0.

N001 gives the explicit generator and divided-power actions on e. Complex linearity gives the same coefficients on b e_i, hence on a_i via iota and on beta_i after applying bar. Consequently x_K beta_0=0, x_K beta_i=(lambda-i+1)beta_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda, y_K beta_i=(i+1)beta_(i+1) for 0<=i<lambda, y_K beta_lambda=0, and h_K beta_i=(lambda-2i)beta_i for i in I. N002 gives preservation of iota(M_R) by E_ij. Define T_ij by the induced lattice action after pulling back through iota and extending scalars using Phi; then T_ij beta_k=beta_i if k=j and 0 otherwise. Transporting the equality E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1)X_(lambda-i)Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j) from N002 gives T_ij=bar(binom(lambda,j))^(-1)X_(lambda-i)^K Y_lambda^K X_lambda^K Y_(lambda-j)^K. This scalar is defined and nonzero, because N002 states that binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R and a unital homomorphism to a field maps units to units.

For any integer r with 0<=r<=lambda, H003 and H001 imply p does not divide r!, so H002 gives r! !=0 in K. The equality r! X_r=x^r on V restricts to the same equality on M by N002 and reduces to r! X_r^K=x_K^r on V_K. Division yields X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r, and the identical argument gives Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r. F001-F003 and these formulas prove all the asserted basis, scalar-extension and operator properties, existentially closing b,a,beta,T. When lambda=0, all factorials and binomial coefficients here are 1. No assumption on algebraic closure of K has been used.

Use H001-H002 for the prime-field/scalar identifications and H005 for the Chevalley construction. N001 and N002 supply the basis-defined matrix units and the restrictions of the lattice operators used in this construction, so all definitions of rho,x_K,y_K,h_K,X_K,Y_K are guarded by established inputs. Choose a basis beta and endomorphisms T with the full properties of N004. In particular dim_K V_K=n>0, so V_K is nonzero.

Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W of V_K and assume L1: W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K. It is then invariant under each nonnegative power of x_K and y_K, including power zero, and under their K-scalar multiples. N004 gives X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r for every 0<=r<=lambda. Every index lambda-i, lambda and lambda-j2 in the formula for T_(i,j2) lies in this interval, and binom(lambda,j2) is nonzero in K. Stability under composition and scalar multiplication now shows that W is invariant under every T_(i,j2), hence under all matrix units since i,j2 were arbitrary.

Split into the exhaustive cases W={0} and W!={0}. In the zero branch temporarily assume L3: W={0}; the desired disjunction follows immediately, so discharge L3 to close that branch. In the nonzero branch temporarily assume L2: W!={0}. Since beta is a basis from N004, there exist w in W, a coefficient family c in K^I, and j in I such that w!=0, w=sum_(i in I)c_i beta_i, and c_j!=0; otherwise all coefficients of every w in W would be zero. Retain this existence as F003 for the next paragraph.

Choose w,c,j from F003. For every i in I, the matrix-unit action in N004 gives T_ij w=c_j beta_i. F002 places this vector in W; division by the nonzero c_j in the field K yields beta_i in W. Thus all basis vectors belong to W and W=V_K. Discharge the nonzero-case assumption L2; together with the zero case this proves W={0} or W=V_K under L1.

Discharge L1 to conclude that invariance under x_K,y_K,h_K implies W={0} or W=V_K, and universally quantify the arbitrary subspace W. Combine this with nonzeroness from F001 to obtain the target conclusion. Since the Chevalley generators span L_K, their invariant subspaces are exactly the L_K-submodules. The endpoint lambda=0 uses a single basis vector with all relevant factorials and binomial coefficients equal to 1. By H003, for p=2 the allowed lambda values are 0 and 1, and the same formulas apply. No step separates h_K-eigenvalues or assumes K algebraically closed.

49: If `M` is an `R`-module and `N` is an `A`-module, then `A`-linear maps `A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] N`
50: correspond to `R` linear maps `M →ₗ[R] N` by composing with `M → A ⊗ M`, `x ↦ 1 ⊗ x`.
51: -/
52: def liftBaseChangeEquiv : (M →ₗ[R] N) ≃ₗ[A] (A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] N) :=
53:   (LinearMap.ringLmapEquivSelf _ _ _).symm.trans (AlgebraTensorModule.lift.equiv _ _ _ _ _ _)
54: 
55: /-- If `N` is an `A` module, we may lift a linear map `M →ₗ[R] N` to `A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] N` -/
56: abbrev liftBaseChange (l : M →ₗ[R] N) : A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] N :=
57:   LinearMap.liftBaseChangeEquiv A l
58:

60: lemma liftBaseChange_tmul (l : M →ₗ[R] N) (x y) : l.liftBaseChange A (x ⊗ₜ y) = x • l y := rfl
61:

69:     (l : M →ₗ[R] N) (l' : N →ₗ[A] P) :
70:       l' ∘ₗ l.liftBaseChange A = (l'.restrictScalars R ∘ₗ l).liftBaseChange A := by

1: # Lean implementation safeguards
2: 
3: Apply these requirements within the accepted NL0 and the fixed Lean interface.
4: They govern implementation, not additional NL0 detail or a weaker Audit B.
5: Use existing library readers and local checking tools; no separate review
6: model, new premise or mandatory lookup of every familiar declaration is needed.
7: 
8: 1. **Check critical library signatures.** Before relying on a critical or
9:    unfamiliar library application, establish its complete type in the pinned
10:    environment, including explicit, implicit and instance binders and all
11:    side conditions. Read the declaration or check a small typed application
12:    when its signature is uncertain. Do not infer the calling convention from
13:    its name or pass an implicit argument as though it were an explicit one.
14:    A previously checked signature in this context need not be looked up again.
15: 2. **Constrain difficult inference.** When coercions or implicit inference
16:    obscure the intended application, give the intermediate fact an explicit
17:    type and supply the relevant named parameters, such as the set, exponent
18:    or ambient space. Prefer this to leaving Lean to discover those choices by
19:    unfolding large definitions. Routine unambiguous arguments can stay
20:    implicit; explicit parameters must preserve the existing target and inputs.
21: 3. **Check conversions before combining them.** When an argument crosses Lean
22:    representations, first establish a small typed conversion fact, then use
23:    it in the main proof. In particular, distinguish `ℝ`, `ℝ≥0` and `ℝ≥0∞`;
24:    check the conversion direction, nonnegativity and any finiteness conditions.
25:    A conversion is not automatically invertible, and matching notation does
26:    not establish equality of differently typed expressions. Reuse a checked
27:    fact when available. Do not invent another representation, a global helper
28:    requirement or an extra hypothesis just to satisfy this instruction.
29: 4. **Isolate an inference failure.** If compiler feedback identifies a library
30:    application, coercion or expensive inference problem, reduce the next check
31:    to that application or conversion with explicit local types before adding
32:    more proof code. Use `check_auxiliary` in a proof worker, or
33:    `check_lean_types` during preparation when that tool is supplied. Helpers
34:    use only the current allowed inputs and never become new premises. Once
35:    the small check succeeds, integrate the result and recheck the complete
36:    obligation; success of a helper alone does not accept the target.
37: 
38: 5. **Repair after a bounded check.** Native checks have a separate per-call wall
39:    limit, normally 180 seconds, and use the controller-owned 20,000,000 heartbeat budget.
40:    A timeout or heartbeat diagnostic leaves the goal unaccepted and returns
41:    control to the same worker. Inspect the retained candidate and diagnostic,
42:    then check a smaller typed application, conversion or proof fragment before
43:    integrating it. Do not repeat the unchanged expensive candidate or disable
44:    limits to avoid diagnosis. Preserve the target, allowed inputs and proof
45:    requirements; a timeout alone establishes no mathematical gap.
46: 
47: The runtime enforces the per-call wall limit independently of these writing
48: rules. Whole-case and model-stage execution remain unlimited by default.
49: Retain failed attempts and actual diagnostics. Standalone assembly, native
50: trust/signature checks and final machine Audit B remain required.
51: 
52: Before freeze, every complete T declaration must elaborate with exactly its
53: worker parameters, instances and direct inputs. Explicitly supply parameters
54: that their argument types cannot determine; a same-named context variable is
55: not an inference rule. The strict declaration check defines the proposition,
56: without proving it, and rejects unresolved holes and non-proposition goals.
57: `#check` is a useful reader aid, not sufficient declaration acceptance. A proof
58: body cannot resolve a hole in its preceding theorem declaration.
59: 
60: Checked auxiliary propositions receive a `yui_aux_...` name and an explicit
61: application with the existing local parameters/inputs. Reuse these theorems in
62: later auxiliary checks and the final body. The controller retains their actual
63: proof bodies and compiles them into standalone assembly. They are same-node
64: implementation lemmas, not extra assumptions. Read the helper index after a
65: context reset; never rebuild a checked helper merely because a turn ended.
66: 
67: Separate diagnostic printing from proving. `show_term` and similar suggestion
68: output may spend substantial time after the proof tactic runs. If that diagnostic
69: wrapper is implicated, check the same proof without it; only the new successful
70: check establishes acceptance. Do not ignore an unsuccessful process exit. If
71: small helpers pass but a monolithic body exhausts resources, retain the separate
72: checked helper declarations and compose them rather than repeatedly copying
73: their bodies into a growing proof.

import Mathlib
open scoped TensorProduct
noncomputable section
namespace Reduction
def loc (p : ℕ) : Subring ℚ :=
  Subring.closure {q : ℚ | ∃ d : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d ∧ q = (d : ℚ)⁻¹}
instance locComplex (p : ℕ) : Algebra (loc p) ℂ :=
  ((Rat.castHom ℂ).comp (loc p).subtype).toAlgebra
abbrev Ind (l : ℤ) := Fin (l.toNat + 1)
abbrev MR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  (loc p) ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  K ⊗[ℤ] M
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
instance locModule (p : ℕ) : Module (loc p) V := Module.compHom V (algebraMap (loc p) ℂ)
instance locTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (loc p) ℂ V := ⟨fun _ _ _ => mul_smul _ _ _⟩
def iota (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[loc p] V :=
  LinearMap.liftBaseChange (loc p) M.subtype
end Reduction

import Mathlib
open scoped TensorProduct
noncomputable section
namespace Reduction
def loc (p : ℕ) : Subring ℚ :=
  Subring.closure {q : ℚ | ∃ d : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d ∧ q = (d : ℚ)⁻¹}
instance locComplex (p : ℕ) : Algebra (loc p) ℂ :=
  ((Rat.castHom ℂ).comp (loc p).subtype).toAlgebra
abbrev Ind (l : ℤ) := Fin (l.toNat + 1)
abbrev MR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  (loc p) ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  K ⊗[ℤ] M
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
instance locModule (p : ℕ) : Module (loc p) V := Module.compHom V (algebraMap (loc p) ℂ)
instance locTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (loc p) ℂ V := ⟨fun _ _ _ => mul_smul _ _ _⟩
def iota (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[loc p] V :=
  LinearMap.liftBaseChange (loc p) M.subtype
end Reduction
types: ∀ (b : Basis (Fin 2) ℂ V) (i j : Fin 2), LinearMap.smulRight (b.coord j) (b i) = (0 : Module.End ℂ V)
∀ (f : Module.End ℤ M), f.baseChange K = f.baseChange K

namespace Reduction
def loc (p : ℕ) : Subring ℚ :=
  Subring.closure {q : ℚ | ∃ d : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d ∧ q = (d : ℚ)⁻¹}
instance locComplex (p : ℕ) : Algebra (loc p) ℂ :=
  ((Rat.castHom ℂ).comp (loc p).subtype).toAlgebra
abbrev Ind (l : ℤ) := Fin (l.toNat + 1)
abbrev MR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  (loc p) ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  K ⊗[ℤ] M
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
instance locModule (p : ℕ) : Module (loc p) V := Module.compHom V (algebraMap (loc p) ℂ)
instance locTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (loc p) ℂ V := ⟨fun _ _ _ => mul_smul _ _ _⟩
def iota (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[loc p] V :=
  LinearMap.liftBaseChange (loc p) M.subtype

abbrev SL := LieAlgebra.SpecialLinear.sl (Fin 2) ℂ
def divided (a : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • a ^ r
def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
def stable {A W : Type*} [Semiring A] [AddCommMonoid W] [Module A W]
    (U : Submodule A W) (f : Module.End A W) : Prop := ∀ w ∈ U, f w ∈ U
def matrixUnit {A W ι : Type*} [Semiring A] [AddCommMonoid W] [Module A W]
    (b : Basis ι A W) (i j : ι) : Module.End A W :=
  LinearMap.smulRight (b.coord j) (b i)
def Jcoord (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) :
    Submodule (loc p) ℂ :=
  (iota p M).range.comap (LinearMap.smulRight (LinearMap.id : ℂ →ₗ[loc p] ℂ) (e y v i))
structure IntegralOps (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) where
  ix : Module.End ℤ M
  iy : Module.End ℤ M
  ih : Module.End ℤ M
  iX : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
  iY : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
  ix_spec : ∀ m : M, (ix m : V) = x m
  iy_spec : ∀ m : M, (iy m : V) = y m
  ih_spec : ∀ m : M, (ih m : V) = h m
  iX_spec : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), (iX r m : V) = divided x r m
  iY_spec : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), (iY r m : V) = divided y r m
def admissible (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  (∃ (ι : Type) (_ : Fintype ι) (a : Basis ι ℤ M) (b : Basis ι ℂ V),
    ∀ i, (a i : V) = b i) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), divided x r m ∈ M ∧ divided y r m ∈ M)
def highestModule (l : ℤ) (act : SL →ₗ⁅ℂ⁆ Module.End ℂ V) (x h : SL) : Prop :=
  FiniteDimensional ℂ V ∧ Module.finrank ℂ V = l.toNat + 1 ∧ Nontrivial V ∧
  (∀ U : Submodule ℂ V, (∀ z : SL, stable U (act z)) → U = ⊥ ∨ U = ⊤) ∧
  ∃ w : V, w ≠ 0 ∧ act x w = 0 ∧ act h w = (l : ℂ) • w
def chevallley (x y h : SL) : Prop :=
  IsSl2Triple h x y ∧ Submodule.span ℂ ({x, y, h} : Set SL) = ⊤
def strings (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  (∀ t : ℕ, h ((y ^ t) v) = ((l : ℂ) - 2 * (t : ℂ)) • (y ^ t) v) ∧
  ∀ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t → x ((y ^ t) v) =
    ((t : ℂ) * ((l : ℂ) - (t : ℂ) + 1)) • (y ^ (t - 1)) v
def generatorFormulas {A W : Type*} [Field A] [AddCommGroup W] [Module A W]
    (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End A W) (f : ℕ → W) : Prop :=
  x (f 0) = 0 ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, i < l.toNat → x (f (i+1)) = ((l : A) - (i : A)) • f i) ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, i < l.toNat → y (f i) = ((i : A) + 1) • f (i+1)) ∧
  y (f l.toNat) = 0 ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ l.toNat → h (f i) = ((l : A) - 2 * (i : A)) • f i)
def basisFacts (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  0 < l.toNat + 1 ∧ Fintype.card (Ind l) = l.toNat + 1 ∧
  (∃ b : Basis (Ind l) ℂ V, ∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) ∧
  strings l x y h v ∧
  (∀ t : ℕ, l.toNat + 1 ≤ t → (y ^ t) v = 0) ∧
  generatorFormulas l x y h (e y v) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (i : Ind l),
    divided x r (e y v i.val) =
      if r ≤ i.val then (Nat.choose (l.toNat - i.val + r) r : ℂ) • e y v (i.val-r) else 0) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (i : Ind l),
    divided y r (e y v i.val) =
      if i.val + r ≤ l.toNat then (Nat.choose (i.val+r) r : ℂ) • e y v (i.val+r) else 0)
end Reduction

15: If `G` is a rank `d` free `ℤ`-module, then `G/nG` is a finite group of cardinality `n ^ d`.
16: -/
17: 
18: @[expose] public section
19: 
20: open Finsupp Function Module
21: 
22: variable {G H M : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] {n : ℕ}
23: 
24: variable (G n) in
25: /-- `ModN G n` denotes the quotient of `G` by multiples of `n` -/
26: abbrev ModN : Type _ := G ⧸ LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)
27: 
28: namespace ModN
29: 
30: instance : Module (ZMod n) (ModN G n) := QuotientAddGroup.zmodModule (by simp)
31: 
32: set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
33: /-- The universal property of `ModN G n` in terms of monoids: Monoid homomorphisms from `ModN G n`
34: are the same as monoid homomorphisms from `G` whose values are `n`-torsion. -/
35: protected def liftEquiv [AddMonoid M] : (ModN G n →+ M) ≃ {φ : G →+ M // ∀ g, n • φ g = 0} where
36:   toFun f := ⟨f.comp (QuotientAddGroup.mk' _), fun g ↦ by
37:     let Gn : AddSubgroup G := (LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)).toAddSubgroup
38:     suffices n • g ∈ (QuotientAddGroup.mk' Gn).ker by
39:       simp only [AddMonoidHom.coe_comp, comp_apply, ← map_nsmul]
40:       change f (QuotientAddGroup.mk' Gn (n • g)) = 0 -- Can we avoid `change`?
41:       rw [this, map_zero]
42:     simp [QuotientAddGroup.ker_mk', Gn]⟩
43:   invFun φ := QuotientAddGroup.lift _ φ <| by rintro - ⟨g, rfl⟩; simpa using φ.property g
44:   left_inv f := by
45:     ext x
46:     induction x using QuotientAddGroup.induction_on
47:     rfl -- Should `simp` suffice here?
48:   right_inv φ := by aesop
49: 
50: /-- The universal property of `ModN G n` in terms of `ZMod n`-modules: `ZMod n`-linear maps from
51: `ModN G n` are the same as monoid homomorphisms from `G` whose values are `n`-torsion. -/
52: protected def liftEquiv' [AddCommGroup H] [Module (ZMod n) H] :
53:     (ModN G n →ₗ[ZMod n] H) ≃ {φ : G →+ H // ∀ g, n • φ g = 0} :=
54:   (AddMonoidHom.toZModLinearMapEquiv n).symm.toEquiv.trans ModN.liftEquiv
55: 
56: variable (n) in
57: /-- The quotient map `G → G / nG`. -/
58: def mkQ : G →+ ModN G n := (LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)).mkQ
59: 
60: variable [NeZero n]
61: 
62: set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
63: /-- Given a free module `G` over `ℤ`, construct the corresponding basis
64: of `G / ⟨n⟩` over `ℤ / nℤ`. -/
65: noncomputable def basis {ι : Type*} (b : Basis ι ℤ G) : Basis ι (ZMod n) (ModN G n) := by
66:   set ψ : G →+ G := zsmulAddGroupHom n
67:   set nG := LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)
68:   set H := G ⧸ nG
69:   set φ : G →ₗ[ℤ] H := nG.mkQ
70:   let mod : (ι →₀ ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ] (ι →₀ ZMod n) := mapRange.linearMap (Int.castAddHom _).toIntLinearMap
71:   let f : G →ₗ[ℤ] (ι →₀ ℤ) := b.repr
72:   have hker : nG ≤ LinearMap.ker (mod.comp f) := by
73:     rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
74:     ext b
75:     simp [mod, f]
76:   let g : H →ₗ[ℤ] (ι →₀ ZMod n) := nG.liftQ (mod.comp f) hker
77:   refine ⟨.ofBijective (g.toAddMonoidHom.toZModLinearMap n) ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
78:   · rw [AddMonoidHom.coe_toZModLinearMap, LinearMap.toAddMonoidHom_coe, injective_iff_map_eq_zero,
79:       nG.mkQ_surjective.forall]
80:     intro x hx
81:     simp only [Submodule.mkQ_apply, g] at hx
82:     rw [Submodule.liftQ_apply] at hx
83:     replace hx : ∀ b, ↑n ∣ f x b := by
84:       simpa [mod, DFunLike.ext_iff, ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd] using! hx

import Mathlib
open scoped TensorProduct
open Module
attribute [local instance 100] LieRing.ofAssociativeRing
noncomputable section
namespace Reduction
def loc (p : ℕ) : Subring ℚ :=
  Subring.closure {q : ℚ | ∃ d : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d ∧ q = (d : ℚ)⁻¹}
instance locComplex (p : ℕ) : Algebra (loc p) ℂ :=
  ((Rat.castHom ℂ).comp (loc p).subtype).toAlgebra
abbrev Ind (l : ℤ) := Fin (l.toNat + 1)
abbrev MR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  (loc p) ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  K ⊗[ℤ] M
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
instance locModule (p : ℕ) : Module (loc p) V := Module.compHom V (algebraMap (loc p) ℂ)
instance locTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (loc p) ℂ V := ⟨fun _ _ _ => mul_smul _ _ _⟩
def iota (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[loc p] V :=
  LinearMap.liftBaseChange (loc p) M.subtype

abbrev SL := LieAlgebra.SpecialLinear.sl (Fin 2) ℂ
def divided (a : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • a ^ r
def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
def stable {A W : Type*} [Semiring A] [AddCommMonoid W] [Module A W]
    (U : Submodule A W) (f : Module.End A W) : Prop := ∀ w ∈ U, f w ∈ U
def matrixUnit {A W ι : Type*} [Semiring A] [AddCommMonoid W] [Module A W]
    (b : Basis ι A W) (i j : ι) : Module.End A W :=
  LinearMap.smulRight (b.coord j) (b i)
def Jcoord (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) :
    Submodule (loc p) ℂ :=
  (iota p M).range.comap (LinearMap.smulRight (LinearMap.id : ℂ →ₗ[loc p] ℂ) (e y v i))
structure IntegralOps (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) where
  ix : Module.End ℤ M
  iy : Module.End ℤ M
  ih : Module.End ℤ M
  iX : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
  iY : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
  ix_spec : ∀ m : M, (ix m : V) = x m
  iy_spec : ∀ m : M, (iy m : V) = y m
  ih_spec : ∀ m : M, (ih m : V) = h m
  iX_spec : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), (iX r m : V) = divided x r m
  iY_spec : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), (iY r m : V) = divided y r m
def admissible (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  (∃ (ι : Type) (_ : Fintype ι) (a : Basis ι ℤ M) (b : Basis ι ℂ V),
    ∀ i, (a i : V) = b i) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), divided x r m ∈ M ∧ divided y r m ∈ M)
def highestModule (l : ℤ) (act : SL →ₗ⁅ℂ⁆ Module.End ℂ V) (x h : SL) : Prop :=
  FiniteDimensional ℂ V ∧ Module.finrank ℂ V = l.toNat + 1 ∧ Nontrivial V ∧
  (∀ U : Submodule ℂ V, (∀ z : SL, stable U (act z)) → U = ⊥ ∨ U = ⊤) ∧
  ∃ w : V, w ≠ 0 ∧ act x w = 0 ∧ act h w = (l : ℂ) • w
def chevallley (x y h : SL) : Prop :=
  IsSl2Triple h x y ∧ Submodule.span ℂ ({x, y, h} : Set SL) = ⊤
def strings (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  (∀ t : ℕ, h ((y ^ t) v) = ((l : ℂ) - 2 * (t : ℂ)) • (y ^ t) v) ∧
  ∀ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t → x ((y ^ t) v) =
    ((t : ℂ) * ((l : ℂ) - (t : ℂ) + 1)) • (y ^ (t - 1)) v
def generatorFormulas {A W : Type*} [Field A] [AddCommGroup W] [Module A W]
    (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End A W) (f : ℕ → W) : Prop :=
  x (f 0) = 0 ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, i < l.toNat → x (f (i+1)) = ((l : A) - (i : A)) • f i) ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, i < l.toNat → y (f i) = ((i : A) + 1) • f (i+1)) ∧
  y (f l.toNat) = 0 ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ l.toNat → h (f i) = ((l : A) - 2 * (i : A)) • f i)
def basisFacts (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  0 < l.toNat + 1 ∧ Fintype.card (Ind l) = l.toNat + 1 ∧
  (∃ b : Basis (Ind l) ℂ V, ∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) ∧
  strings l x y h v ∧
  (∀ t : ℕ, l.toNat + 1 ≤ t → (y ^ t) v = 0) ∧
  generatorFormulas l x y h (e y v) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (i : Ind l),
    divided x r (e y v i.val) =
      if r ≤ i.val then (Nat.choose (l.toNat - i.val + r) r : ℂ) • e y v (i.val-r) else 0) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (i : Ind l),
    divided y r (e y v i.val) =
      if i.val + r ≤ l.toNat then (Nat.choose (i.val+r) r : ℂ) • e y v (i.val+r) else 0)

instance locRatComplexTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (loc p) ℚ ℂ :=
  IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' rfl
def locSpec (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ q : ℚ, q ∈ loc p ↔ ∃ a d : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (d : ℚ)
def latticeFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  locSpec p ∧ Nonempty (IntegralOps x y h M) ∧
  (∀ A : IntegralOps x y h M,
    A.ih * A.ix - A.ix * A.ih = (2 : ℤ) • A.ix ∧
    A.ih * A.iy - A.iy * A.ih = (-2 : ℤ) • A.iy ∧
    A.ix * A.iy - A.iy * A.ix = A.ih) ∧
  Function.Injective (iota p M) ∧
  Nonempty (Basis (Ind l) (loc p) (MR p M)) ∧
  Module.finrank (loc p) (MR p M) = l.toNat + 1 ∧
  Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (iota p M)) = ⊤ ∧
  ∀ (r : ℕ) (z : V), z ∈ (iota p M).range →
    divided x r z ∈ (iota p M).range ∧ divided y r z ∈ (iota p M).range
def matrixFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ b : Basis (Ind l) ℂ V, (∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) →
  ∀ i j : Ind l,
    IsUnit (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : loc p) ∧
    (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : ℚ)⁻¹ ∈ loc p ∧
    (∀ z ∈ (iota p M).range, matrixUnit b i j z ∈ (iota p M).range) ∧
    matrixUnit b i j = (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : ℂ)⁻¹ •
      (divided x (l.toNat-i.val) * divided y l.toNat * divided x l.toNat * divided y (l.toNat-j.val)) ∧
    divided y l.toNat * divided x l.toNat = matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) (Fin.last l.toNat) ∧
    divided x (l.toNat-i.val) * matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) (Fin.last l.toNat) =
      matrixUnit b i (Fin.last l.toNat) ∧
    matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) (Fin.last l.toNat) * divided y (l.toNat-j.val) =
      (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : ℂ) • matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) j
def localizationFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  latticeFacts p l x y h M ∧ matrixFacts p l x y v M
def coordinateFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : Ind l, Jcoord p M y v i.val = Jcoord p M y v 0) ∧
  Jcoord p M y v 0 ≠ ⊥ ∧ (Jcoord p M y v 0).FG ∧
  ∃ d : (Ind l → Jcoord p M y v 0) ≃ₗ[loc p] (iota p M).range,
    ∀ c, (d c : V) = ∑ i : Ind l, (c i : ℂ) • e y v i.val
def rationalMu (p : ℕ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) :
    ℚ ⊗[loc p] (Jcoord p M y v 0) →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ :=
  LinearMap.liftBaseChange ℚ (Jcoord p M y v 0).subtype
def rationalFacts (p : ℕ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  FiniteDimensional ℚ (ℚ ⊗[loc p] (Jcoord p M y v 0)) ∧
  Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[loc p] (Jcoord p M y v 0)) = 1 ∧
  Function.Injective (rationalMu p y v M)
def principalFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ b : ℂ, b ≠ 0 ∧ b ∈ Jcoord p M y v 0 ∧
    Jcoord p M y v 0 = Submodule.span (loc p) ({b} : Set ℂ) ∧
    ∃ a : Basis (Ind l) (loc p) (MR p M), ∀ i, iota p M (a i) = b • e y v i.val
def commonFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  coordinateFacts p l y v M ∧ rationalFacts p y v M ∧ principalFacts p l y v M
def scalarFacts (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (bar : loc p →+* K) (eps : ZMod p →+* K),
    (∀ (a d : ℤ) (hd : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d) (r : loc p),
      (r : ℚ) = (a : ℚ) / (d : ℚ) → bar r = (a : K) / (d : K)) ∧
    (letI : Algebra (loc p) K := bar.toAlgebra
     letI : Algebra (ZMod p) K := eps.toAlgebra
     ∃ (Phi : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[loc p] MR p M))
       (Psi : (K ⊗[loc p] MR p M) ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[ZMod p] ModN (MR p M) p)),
       (∀ (c : K) (m : M), Phi (c ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = c ⊗ₜ[loc p] (1 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) ∧
       (∀ (c : K) (s : loc p) (m : M),
         Phi.symm (c ⊗ₜ[loc p] (s ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) = (c * bar s) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) ∧
       (∀ (c : K) (u : MR p M), Psi (c ⊗ₜ[loc p] u) = c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] ModN.mkQ p u) ∧
       (∀ (c : K) (u : MR p M), Psi.symm (c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] ModN.mkQ p u) = c ⊗ₜ[loc p] u) ∧
       ∀ f : Module.End ℤ M,
         Phi.toLinearMap.comp (f.baseChange K) =
           ((f.baseChange (loc p)).baseChange K).comp Phi.toLinearMap ∧
         ∃ F : Module.End (ZMod p) (ModN (MR p M) p),
           (∀ u : MR p M, F (ModN.mkQ p u) = ModN.mkQ p (f.baseChange (loc p) u)) ∧
           Psi.toLinearMap.comp ((f.baseChange (loc p)).baseChange K) =
             (F.baseChange K).comp Psi.toLinearMap)
def extendBasis {A W : Type*} [Semiring A] [AddCommMonoid W] [Module A W]
    (l : ℤ) (b : Basis (Ind l) A W) (i : ℕ) : W :=
  if hi : i < l.toNat+1 then b ⟨i,hi⟩ else 0
def reductionWitness (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K]
    {x y h : Module.End ℂ V} {M : Submodule ℤ V} (A : IntegralOps x y h M)
    (beta : Basis (Ind l) K (VK K M)) (T : Ind l → Ind l → Module.End K (VK K M)) : Prop :=
  Module.finrank K (VK K M) = l.toNat+1 ∧ 0 < l.toNat+1 ∧
  generatorFormulas l (A.ix.baseChange K) (A.iy.baseChange K) (A.ih.baseChange K) (extendBasis l beta) ∧
  (∀ i j k : Ind l, T i j (beta k) = if k = j then beta i else 0) ∧
  (∀ i j : Ind l, (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : K) ≠ 0 ∧
    T i j = (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : K)⁻¹ •
      ((A.iX (l.toNat-i.val)).baseChange K * (A.iY l.toNat).baseChange K *
        (A.iX l.toNat).baseChange K * (A.iY (l.toNat-j.val)).baseChange K)) ∧
  ∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ l.toNat →
    (r.factorial : K) ≠ 0 ∧
    (A.iX r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (A.ix.baseChange K)^r ∧
    (A.iY r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (A.iy.baseChange K)^r
def reductionFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K]
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  scalarFacts p K M ∧
  ∀ A : IntegralOps x y h M, ∃ beta T, reductionWitness p l K A beta T
def invariantFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K]
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial (VK K M) ∧
  ∀ A : IntegralOps x y h M, ∃ beta T, reductionWitness p l K A beta T ∧
    ∀ W : Submodule K (VK K M),
      stable W (A.ix.baseChange K) → stable W (A.iy.baseChange K) →
      stable W (A.ih.baseChange K) → ∀ i j : Ind l, stable W (T i j)
def endpoint (K : Type*) [Field K] (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : IntegralOps x y h M, Nontrivial (VK K M) ∧
    ∀ W : Submodule K (VK K M),
      stable W (A.ix.baseChange K) → stable W (A.iy.baseChange K) →
      stable W (A.ih.baseChange K) → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
end Reduction

49: /-- The rank of a module as a natural number.
50: 
51: For a finite-dimensional vector space `V` over a field `k`, `Module.finrank k V` is equal to
52: the dimension of `V` over `k`.
53: 
54: For a general module `M` over a ring `R`, `Module.finrank R M` is defined to be the supremum of the
55: cardinalities of the `R`-linearly independent subsets of `M`, if this supremum is finite. It is
56: defined by convention to be `0` if this supremum is infinite. See `Module.rank` for a
57: cardinal-valued version where infinite rank modules have rank an infinite cardinal.
58: 
59: Note that if `R` is not a field then there can exist modules `M` with `¬(Module.Finite R M)` but
60: `finrank R M ≠ 0`. For example `ℚ` has `finrank` equal to `1` over `ℤ`, because the nonempty
61: `ℤ`-linearly independent subsets of `ℚ` are precisely the nonzero singletons. -/

def divided (a : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=

structure IntegralOps (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) where

  iY : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M

    A.ix * A.iy - A.iy * A.ix = A.ih) ∧
  Function.Injective (iota p M) ∧
  Nonempty (Basis (Ind l) (loc p) (MR p M)) ∧
  Module.finrank (loc p) (MR p M) = l.toNat + 1 ∧
  Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (iota p M)) = ⊤ ∧
  ∀ (r : ℕ) (z : V), z ∈ (iota p M).range →
    divided x r z ∈ (iota p M).range ∧ divided y r z ∈ (iota p M).range
def matrixFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ b : Basis (Ind l) ℂ V, (∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) →
  ∀ i j : Ind l,
    IsUnit (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : loc p) ∧
    (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : ℚ)⁻¹ ∈ loc p ∧
    (∀ z ∈ (iota p M).range, matrixUnit b i j z ∈ (iota p M).range) ∧
    matrixUnit b i j = (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : ℂ)⁻¹ •
      (divided x (l.toNat-i.val) * divided y l.toNat * divided x l.toNat * divided y (l.toNat-j.val)) ∧
    divided y l.toNat * divided x l.toNat = matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) (Fin.last l.toNat) ∧
    divided x (l.toNat-i.val) * matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) (Fin.last l.toNat) =
      matrixUnit b i (Fin.last l.toNat) ∧
    matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) (Fin.last l.toNat) * divided y (l.toNat-j.val) =
      (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : ℂ) • matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) j
def localizationFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  latticeFacts p l x y h M ∧ matrixFacts p l x y v M
def coordinateFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : Ind l, Jcoord p M y v i.val = Jcoord p M y v 0) ∧
  Jcoord p M y v 0 ≠ ⊥ ∧ (Jcoord p M y v 0).FG ∧
  ∃ d : (Ind l → Jcoord p M y v 0) ≃ₗ[loc p] (iota p M).range,
    ∀ c, (d c : V) = ∑ i : Ind l, (c i : ℂ) • e y v i.val
def rationalMu (p : ℕ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) :
    ℚ ⊗[loc p] (Jcoord p M y v 0) →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ :=
  LinearMap.liftBaseChange ℚ (Jcoord p M y v 0).subtype
def rationalFacts (p : ℕ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  FiniteDimensional ℚ (ℚ ⊗[loc p] (Jcoord p M y v 0)) ∧
  Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[loc p] (Jcoord p M y v 0)) = 1 ∧
  Function.Injective (rationalMu p y v M)
def principalFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ b : ℂ, b ≠ 0 ∧ b ∈ Jcoord p M y v 0 ∧
    Jcoord p M y v 0 = Submodule.span (loc p) ({b} : Set ℂ) ∧
    ∃ a : Basis (Ind l) (loc p) (MR p M), ∀ i, iota p M (a i) = b • e y v i.val
def commonFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  coordinateFacts p l y v M ∧ rationalFacts p y v M ∧ principalFacts p l y v M
def scalarFacts (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (bar : loc p →+* K) (eps : ZMod p →+* K),
    (∀ (a d : ℤ) (hd : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d) (r : loc p),
      (r : ℚ) = (a : ℚ) / (d : ℚ) → bar r = (a : K) / (d : K)) ∧
    (letI : Algebra (loc p) K := bar.toAlgebra
     letI : Algebra (ZMod p) K := eps.toAlgebra
     ∃ (Phi : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[loc p] MR p M))
       (Psi : (K ⊗[loc p] MR p M) ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[ZMod p] ModN (MR p M) p)),
       (∀ (c : K) (m : M), Phi (c ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = c ⊗ₜ[loc p] (1 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) ∧
       (∀ (c : K) (s : loc p) (m : M),
         Phi.symm (c ⊗ₜ[loc p] (s ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) = (c * bar s) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) ∧
       (∀ (c : K) (u : MR p M), Psi (c ⊗ₜ[loc p] u) = c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] ModN.mkQ p u) ∧
       (∀ (c : K) (u : MR p M), Psi.symm (c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] ModN.mkQ p u) = c ⊗ₜ[loc p] u) ∧
       ∀ f : Module.End ℤ M,
         Phi.toLinearMap.comp (f.baseChange K) =
           ((f.baseChange (loc p)).baseChange K).comp Phi.toLinearMap ∧
         ∃ F : Module.End (ZMod p) (ModN (MR p M) p),
           (∀ u : MR p M, F (ModN.mkQ p u) = ModN.mkQ p (f.baseChange (loc p) u)) ∧
           Psi.toLinearMap.comp ((f.baseChange (loc p)).baseChange K) =
             (F.baseChange K).comp Psi.toLinearMap)
def extendBasis {A W : Type*} [Semiring A] [AddCommMonoid W] [Module A W]
    (l : ℤ) (b : Basis (Ind l) A W) (i : ℕ) : W :=
  if hi : i < l.toNat+1 then b ⟨i,hi⟩ else 0
def reductionWitness (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K]
    {x y h : Module.End ℂ V} {M : Submodule ℤ V} (A : IntegralOps x y h M)
    (beta : Basis (Ind l) K (VK K M)) (T : Ind l → Ind l → Module.End K (VK K M)) : Prop :=
  Module.finrank K (VK K M) = l.toNat+1 ∧ 0 < l.toNat+1 ∧
  generatorFormulas l (A.ix.baseChange K) (A.iy.baseChange K) (A.ih.baseChange K) (extendBasis l beta) ∧
  (∀ i j k : Ind l, T i j (beta k) = if k = j then beta i else 0) ∧
  (∀ i j : Ind l, (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : K) ≠ 0 ∧
    T i j = (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : K)⁻¹ •
      ((A.iX (l.toNat-i.val)).baseChange K * (A.iY l.toNat).baseChange K *
        (A.iX l.toNat).baseChange K * (A.iY (l.toNat-j.val)).baseChange K)) ∧
  ∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ l.toNat →
    (r.factorial : K) ≠ 0 ∧
    (A.iX r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (A.ix.baseChange K)^r ∧
    (A.iY r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (A.iy.baseChange K)^r
def reductionFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K]
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  scalarFacts p K M ∧
  ∀ A : IntegralOps x y h M, ∃ beta T, reductionWitness p l K A beta T
def invariantFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K]
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial (VK K M) ∧
  ∀ A : IntegralOps x y h M, ∃ beta T, reductionWitness p l K A beta T ∧
    ∀ W : Submodule K (VK K M),
      stable W (A.ix.baseChange K) → stable W (A.iy.baseChange K) →
      stable W (A.ih.baseChange K) → ∀ i j : Ind l, stable W (T i j)
def endpoint (K : Type*) [Field K] (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : IntegralOps x y h M, Nontrivial (VK K M) ∧
    ∀ W : Submodule K (VK K M),
      stable W (A.ix.baseChange K) → stable W (A.iy.baseChange K) →
      stable W (A.ih.baseChange K) → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
end Reduction
